title: How Random Forest Performs So Well? Bias Variance Trade-Off in Random Forest

segments.text: So guys, till now we have taken the basic intuition of random forest that how algorithm works. I have also shown you a step-by-step example. In this video, we will see that why random forest works well? Why its performance is good in comparison to other algorithms? Its reason is hidden in bias variance trade-off. I hope you have read about this topic till now.

If you have not studied, then I will give you a short summary of the whole topic. There are two very important things in machine learning, bias and variance. Basically, in your machine learning, you get an error. Your machine learning model gives an error. So that error is made up of two things. One is bias and the other is variance. What is bias? Bias is when a machine learning model does not give a good result on training data.

It means that your machine learning model did not learn very well in the training process itself. It means that it will not give good results on the training data. It means that its bias will be high. Second is variance. What is variance? Sometimes your machine learning model learns very well on the training data and basically takes the patterns of the training data. Because of which when you give it new data, its performance is not that good.

So basically, if you make any changes in the data, the outcome of your machine learning model will not be good. This is called high variance. So you always have to try in machine learning that you keep low bias. I will write it here. You always need low bias and low variance. But there is a problem. The problem is this, that between these two, between bias and variance,

There is an inverse relationship. If you try to reduce one, then the other one increases. And that is why most of the machine learning algorithms, they struggle with the bias-variance trade-off. If you try to reduce one error, then the other one increases. That's why mostly the machine learning algorithms that you have are defined in two classes. The first class is low bias.

High variance algorithms means an algorithm that is able to give very good results on training data but not able to give good results on new test data. The example of these algorithms is fully grown decision tree. A decision tree where you are not capping the max depth. Fully grown decision tree. Second is SVM also sometimes shows this behavior.

KNN, when your nearest number of neighbors are very less. Then a second class of algorithms is, when you have high bias but low variance. A very good example of this is linear regression. And in certain cases, logistic regression also. But you never get this combination, which you need. Where bias is less and variance is less. Here, random forest helps you. What is the specialty of random forest?

that if you give it a low-bias, high-variance algorithm, then it will convert it into a low-bias, low-variance algorithm. This means that what does random forest do on this type of algorithm? It reduces its variance by keeping its bias as it is. Now let's understand how this happens. So the answer to this is hidden in its working.

I had explained to you how it works. What you do is you take some base models and all these base models are actually decision trees. And these are fully grown decision trees. Fully grown decision trees means everyone is low bias and high variance. Here every model is low bias and high variance. No one will make a mistake on training data and no one will make a mistake on new data. Now what you do is you hold your data. This is your data and its subset.

feed every algorithm. For example, if there were 10,000 rows, then you might be giving everyone 1,000 rows. Now these models are trained. Since these are decision trees internally, the outcome will remain low bias. But let's think what will happen with variance.

So, something interesting happens with variance. Let me give you an example. Suppose you replaced 100 points in 10k points. And how did you replace them? You replaced them with points that are very different, noisy, and outliers. It means you have made changes in the data. Now, obviously, if you had made changes in the data, and you had a single decision tree, then variance would have been high.

But since you are using random forest, collection of trees, what will happen now? Now when you randomly send data, then it will never happen that 100 noisy points will be given to a single decision tree. Because you are drawing randomly, so it is possible that the first one gets 10 noisy points, the second one gets 5, the third one doesn't get even 1, the next one gets 15. So the impact of 100 points,

Earlier, one decision tree had to be tolerated. Now, no decision tree has to be tolerated. So, the impact of the outliers, the impact of noisy points, has now been distributed. And due to distribution, it has become weak. So, that is why, the result that was coming earlier, and the result that is coming after bringing these points, there won't be much difference.

And not much difference means that you have reduced the variety. And because of this, your overall model will be low variance. So in short, random forest performs well because it solves a big problem.

bias-variance trade-off, which says that you can't reduce both bias and variance because there is an inverse relationship between the two. If you reduce bias, variance will increase. If you reduce variance, bias will increase. But by using this technique, you are able to reduce variance while keeping bias low. I hope you are able to understand this whole thing. And your model is able to capture the true nature of the data. What is the true nature of the data? That it is inside the yellow points and purple points. It is telling exactly the same thing. And that is why Random Forest is such a great algorithm. Because it converts a low-bias, high-variance algorithm into a low-bias, low-variance algorithm.
